describe: Gulf Coastal Plain: 19 beds, dipping 0.20° to the S.
notes: Regional heat flow ~45 mW/m²; kilometres of light sediment and salt below.
A E-W growth fault steps the beds down 76 m toward the sea; water seeps along it. Seismic: thickening beds on the down side.
A salt dome 660 m across, beds ringing it: caprock about 12 m down, then salt that dissolves so the ground sinks into a hollow or lake. Strong gravity low; sulfur in the caprock.
A salt dome 1.0 km across, beds ringing it: caprock about 17 m down, then salt that dissolves so the ground sinks into a hollow or lake. Strong gravity low; sulfur in the caprock.
5 soluble beds (limestone, gypsum, chalk): where exposed, streams lose water into the ground and the rock slowly dissolves.
